correctness.rationale: For every n>=2, spectral projectors onto Walsh weight k levels are mutually orthogonal. The two-site evaluation Gram determinant is positive at each 1<=k<=n-1 iff 1<=d<n: both signs occur among k-subsets. At d=n both columns are collinear at all k; endpoints k=0,n are always rank one. Summing proves the bright dimensions; Gram pseudoinverses recover each matrix element. Non-Hermitian-loss Hermitian-dissipativity and reducing dark/bright spaces ensure the bright semigroup tends to zero for all positive loss rates. Independent spectral/Krylov numerical checks cover n=2..6 and independent full decay checks unequal rates at n=2..4. Finite checks are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Two local absorbing sites constitute a natural minimal control/design choice. The result exactly resolves the Hamming-distance dependence of permanent quantum-dark-state protection for all binary hypercube dimensions: the unique antipodal separation is entirely redundant, while every other separation achieves the same maximal captured dimension 2n. The site-resolved Krawtchouk formula and full bright operator quantify heterogeneous input states, allowing genuine detector placement analysis. This is an infinite-family structural classification with a nontrivial graph-specific proof, not a numerical census or an unmotivated parameter slice.
